title: Arizona utility evidence for semiconductor and AI infrastructure power capacity
question: Which utility records show real power capacity for semiconductor and AI infrastructure?
why_it_matters: State-level electricity baselines are useful, but power availability for fabs, suppliers, and compute infrastructure depends on utility planning, interconnection, rates, service territory, and facility load evidence.
current_support: FTFN has EIA Arizona electricity context, ACC utility-regulation and eDocket layers, SRP's named 2025 Integrated System Plan Actions Progress Report, the November 2025 E-67 large-load price plan, Project Huckleberry's completed Meta service trail, and Project Baccara's approved CEC, reported 4-1 conditional military-compatibility permit vote, and proposed air permit for approximately 700 MW of planned on-site generation.
missing_evidence: named semiconductor-customer tariff treatment and facilities charges
executed electric-service agreements and service studies
candidate_records: specific ACC utility docket or order
SRP or APS customer-specific service agreement or energization record
semiconductor facility load or service agreement evidence
Project Baccara final air permit, precise Plan of Development, service, construction, interconnection, occupancy, and operating records
next_action: Follow the named Meta energization example and Project Baccara's conditional permit stack into final air and plan approvals, disclosed load, service agreements, construction, interconnection, occupancy, and operating evidence, and still select a semiconductor-customer service record before making TSMC or corridor-wide capacity claims.
notes: Phase 55C advances Project Baccara into a conditional county and proposed air-permit stage. The gap remains unresolved because the records do not establish final air approval, service, construction, interconnection, occupancy, operating consumption, TSMC service, regional spare capacity, or corridor-wide readiness.
